answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted, time-decaying reputation: each agent locks a bond and earns trust only through completed work attested by established peers. A fresh identity starts at zero and cannot wander into deals until it builds history, so creating thousands of fakes means locking a bond for each one. Like a glacier carving a valley slowly, trust accumulates gradually and cannot be rushed, while a tundra of idle fake accounts earns nothing and forfeits bonds if caught cheating — making a 10,000-identity attack cost 10,000 bonds plus months of waiting.
